title: An error enum of your own
description:
Write an error type and a function that uses it:

```rust
enum CountError { Empty, NotANumber(String), TooBig(u64) }
fn parse_count(text: &str) -> Result<u32, CountError>
```

- `parse_count` trims the text; empty text is `Empty`; text that is not a whole number of 0 or more is `NotANumber` with the trimmed text; a number above 10,000 is `TooBig` with the number.
- `CountError` derives `Debug` and `PartialEq`, implements `Display` with the messages `no count given`, `"abc" is not a count` (with the quotes) and `12000 is more than 10000`, and implements `std::error::Error`.
hints: Give each failure a variant, then implement `fmt::Display` with one `write!` per variant, and add the empty `impl std::error::Error for CountError {}` (lesson 8.01).
Parse into a `u64` first, so very large numbers become `TooBig` instead of failing to parse, then convert to `u32` after the range check.
